candidate.blueprint_locator: 2026 NCLEX-RN Test Plan, Reduction of Risk Potential, printed p.13 / PDF p.17
candidate.educational_objective: Explain why cystatin C can help assess GFR when creatinine is confounded by abnormal muscle mass.

options.A: It provides an alternative index of glomerular filtration that is less tied to skeletal muscle mass than creatinine
options.B: It measures liver synthetic function rather than kidney filtration
options.C: It is useful only when muscle mass is normal
options.D: It is unrelated to glomerular filtration rate

candidate.rationale: Mayo Clinic Laboratories describes cystatin C as an index of GFR that can be useful when serum creatinine may be misleading, including in people with atypical muscle mass. Unlike creatinine, cystatin C production is not linked to skeletal muscle mass in the same way.
candidate.source_claim_supported: Supports cystatin C as an index of GFR especially when serum creatinine is misleading due to atypical muscle mass.
candidate.source_document_title: Cystatin C with Estimated Glomerular Filtration Rate (eGFR), Serum (CSTCE)
candidate.source_locator: Useful For; Clinical/interpretive rationale for use when creatinine may be misleading
candidate.stem: A provider orders cystatin C with eGFR for a client whose very low muscle mass may make creatinine-based estimates less reliable. Why is cystatin C useful in this situation?
